title: Stream Exchange Bridge: backpressure scenarios and ergonomic TS adapter
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Goal: design and implement a lightweight 'stream exchange' adapter in the TypeScript SDK that lets consumers seamlessly use AsyncIterator-based code and Web Streams (ReadableStream) with consistent backpressure, cancellation, and retry semantics. The adapter should be ergonomic for both browser and Node runtimes, handle partial-frame resume on transient network errors, and provide minimal API surface for common patterns (for-await, stream.pipeTo, dual-consumption).
acceptance_criteria: 1) Provide a documented adapter API that converts between AsyncIterator<Uint8Array|string|Event> and ReadableStream with preserved backpressure semantics. 2) Retry behavior: transient network errors cause automatic resume where possible (idempotent tokens) and fall back to model-variant routing on persistent failures. 3) Cancellation: calling .return() on the iterator or cancel() on the ReadableStream will propagate abort to the underlying request and stop KV cache growth. 4) Tests: unit + integration tests for Node (stream.Readable) and Browser (ReadableStream) showing pause/resume under load, ordering guarantees, and proper memory usage. 5) Examples: three new SDK snippets (for-await, web-streams pipeline, dual consumer demo) added to docs repo and examples folder.
comments: 2026-02-12 - Ava Martinez: Created ticket after spike found multiple edge cases in duel consumption and backpressure mismatch between for-await and ReadableStream.pipeTo. Initial scope includes adapter surface and examples; not covering binary framing codec changes in this ticket.

2026-02-19 - Rohan Singh: Spike results attached. Observed that Node's stream.Readable highWaterMark + async iterator buffering can cause >2x memory in synthetic workloads. Proposed solution: expose a tunable chunker that yields control when buffer exceeds configured watermark.

2026-02-24 - Design review (Lena Cho): Agreed to keep API minimal: expose fromAsyncIterator() and toAsyncIterator() helpers on the SDK streaming export. Recommended default names: sdk.stream.toWeb and sdk.stream.fromWeb. Also requested example patterns for dual consumer and backpressure bridging.

2026-03-03 - Engineering notes: Implemented prototype for fromAsyncIterator -> ReadableStream with controller.desiredSize checks for backpressure. Node adaptation uses stream.Readable.from with custom highWaterMark wiring. Found race when iterator.return() resolves after underlying request aborted; added sentinel abort token to avoid resuming stale requests.

2026-03-06 - PR #1473: Initial adapter + unit tests. Tests cover ordering and cancellation for small payloads. Reviewer Samir Patel requested clearer error propagation and more integration tests against the hosted API mock.

2026-03-09 - Integration run: ran stress harness (100 concurrent streams, variable payload sizes) in CI. Memory spike reduced by ~45% vs previous naive adapter. However, intermittent duplicate 'end' events when network retries were enabled; root cause: retryer attempted to re-open stream without checking last-offset. Added stateful resume token and idempotency key to request metadata.
2026-03-12 - UX/Docs follow-up: Drafted three example snippets and playground demos. Need PM review for copy and to confirm this fits examples taxonomy. Created docs PR #1509.

2026-03-14 - Rohan Singh: Addressed Samir's feedback; consolidated errors into SDK StreamError type with codes (CANCELLED, NETWORK_RETRY_EXHAUSTED, PROTOCOL_MISMATCH). Added explicit guidance in examples on when automatic resume is safe vs when apps should opt into replay semantics. Marking In Progress; remaining: cross-runtime e2e in real browser and gated rollout plan for clients on Dedicated.

Pending - Ops/Release: Coordinate canary release and telemetry collection for stream-level metrics (idle-time, buffer-usage, retry-count). Need to add roll-forward metric to Console dashboards (cost-by-route during retries).
